subject.title: [Feature]: cron jobs.d/ directory support (one file per job, for NixOS/GitOps declarative setups)

question: Should OpenClaw core own a jobs.d/declarative cron file surface, or should this remain a ClawHub/plugin sync workflow on top of the SQLite cron store?
rationale: Current code and docs intentionally use SQLite rows as the cron runtime store, while the request adds a new file-backed declaration/config surface with compatibility and path-trust implications that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Keep as product design item
options.body: Keep this issue open until a maintainer chooses the core-vs-plugin direction and the required compatibility/security contract.

options.title: Route to ClawHub/plugin sync
options.body: Close or redirect the request if maintainers decide a directory-to-cron sync package is sufficient with current cron APIs and extension seams.

options.title: Sponsor a core declarative sync
options.body: Approve a core design that documents import/sync semantics, preserves SQLite runtime state, and covers doctor, docs, and focused cron tests.

recommendation.title: Keep as product design item
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a maintainer chooses the core-vs-plugin direction and the required compatibility/security contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent SQLite cron persistence migration makes steipete the clearest routing candidate for the storage/product boundary decision.
